- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot sharp upward spikes (e.g., 50→53) and fail to capture the full magnitude of subsequent corrections.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a spike, it prematurely corrects downward, missing the true peak or trough.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days for the first 10–15 days, then converge more closely.
- Model underestimates the true mean of the 30-day window, especially when the true outcome is above 50.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture volatility or sudden reversals in the last 5–7 days.
- When true outcome shows a sharp downward trend, model continues to forecast upward, missing the turn.
- Model overreacts to recent high values, leading to premature downward corrections.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the true outcome is below 50, but systematically biased upward when above 50.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or structural shifts in the 30-day window, especially after a spike.
